lesson.subtitle: Lesson 12 -- What Happened? The Bag That Stayed Behind
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Anthonyo Leão de Souza neto | Lesson 12 -- What Happened?

paras: Dear Mr. de Souza, thank you for your patience yesterday at the airport. Here is what happened, step by step.
Your flight from São Paulo landed at six forty in the morning. Your bag was not on the belt, because it stayed in Lisbon. The connection there was very short.
You waited at belt number seven for forty minutes. Then you talked to our team at the counter, and you filled in a form with your hotel and your phone number.
At eleven, our office in Lisbon called us. They checked the number on your bag tag, and the bag was there, in the right place.
The bag arrived on the next flight, at four in the afternoon. We delivered it to your hotel at seven thirty in the evening, and the front desk signed for it.
We are very sorry for the long day. Finally, one thing for next time: keep one shirt and your medicine in your carry-on bag.

listenings.text: Last Tuesday was the worst travel day of my year. I arrived at the airport early, at five in the morning. The flight was at seven, but at six it changed to nine. I waited. Then it changed to eleven. I waited again. At eleven they canceled it. So I walked to the counter, I asked for a new flight, and I booked a seat on the evening flight. I called my wife, I called the hotel, and I called the office, in that order. The evening flight landed at midnight, and I checked in at the hotel at one in the morning. The room was comfortable, and I was too tired to care. And you know what? My bag arrived with me, on the same flight. That was the good part.

My first day in Tokyo was very simple, and it is my favorite day of that trip. I landed at six in the morning, and I was very tired, so I walked slowly from the hotel to the river. I stopped at a small coffee shop, and the owner talked to me for twenty minutes, with his hands and three words of English. In the afternoon I visited a market, and I tasted eleven things. Eleven. I liked ten of them. In the evening it rained, so I stayed in the hotel. I ordered dinner in the room and I watched the rain on the window. It was a quiet day, and I loved it. Today I do not remember the museums from that trip. I remember the coffee shop.
